responsibilities.name: Nightly Memory Consolidation
responsibilities.instruction: Execute the nightly memory consolidation cycle: prune working memory of completed and stale entries, reconcile long-term Core Memory by retiring outdated facts and promoting durable new ones, and review Deep Truths for behavioral updates.

context.purpose: MEMORY.md is the agent's working scratchpad — loaded into every Cortex prompt as baseline knowledge. It accumulates freely during the day but must be pruned nightly to stay under 2,000 characters. Core Memory in Firestore is the long-term archive — facts that survive across days and weeks. It must also be actively pruned: stale entries retired, contradicted facts superseded, and only genuinely stable new facts promoted. Deep Truths in SOUL.md are behavioral constraints loaded into every prompt — they change rarely and only with strong multi-session evidence.
process: STEP 1 — GATHER WORKING MEMORY: Read the current workspace/MEMORY.md to understand what has accumulated during the day.
STEP 2 — GATHER SESSIONS: Run `session-summary --hours 24 --limit 20` to extract a digest of recent conversations and completed work from the last 24 hours.

STEP 3 — GATHER RECENT CORE MEMORY: Run `core-memory-read --since 30d --limit 20` to pull broadly from recent long-term storage. This shows what the agent has been learning and storing over the past month.

STEP 4 — GATHER FULL ARCHIVE: Run `core-memory-read --category <cat>` for each category (architecture, operations, iam, decisions, patterns, errors) to see the full long-term knowledge base. Identify entries that may be outdated or contradicted by recent work.

STEP 5 — TRIAGE WORKING MEMORY: Classify every entry in MEMORY.md into one of four buckets: (a) ACTIVE — still relevant, keep in MEMORY.md, (b) COMPLETED — task finished or resolved, prune, (c) STALE — outdated information no longer accurate, prune, (d) PROMOTE — stable fact proven across multiple sessions, worthy of Core Memory.

STEP 6 — RECONCILE LONG-TERM MEMORY: Compare recent work (from Steps 1-2) against long-term Core Memory (from Steps 3-4). Identify: (a) CONTRADICTED entries — long-term facts that are no longer true based on recent evidence, (b) OUTDATED entries — facts about versions, endpoints, or configurations that have changed, (c) REDUNDANT entries — multiple entries saying the same thing that can be consolidated, (d) STALE entries — facts not recalled in weeks that are no longer operationally relevant.

STEP 7 — RETIRE STALE LONG-TERM ENTRIES: For each entry identified in Step 6, use `core-memory-retire --id <entry-id> --reason "<specific reason>"` to mark it retired. For entries that need updating rather than retiring, use `core-memory-write --fact "<updated fact>" --category <cat> --supersedes <old-id>`. Maximum 5 retirement/supersede operations per run.

STEP 8 — PROMOTE NEW FACTS: For each PROMOTE item from Step 5, write to Core Memory via `core-memory-write --fact "<fact>" --category <cat> --tags "t1,t2"`. Only promote facts that: appeared in multiple sessions, were confirmed by the operator, or represent stable architectural/operational patterns. Maximum 5 writes per run.

STEP 9 — PRUNE AND REWRITE WORKING MEMORY: Rewrite MEMORY.md keeping only ACTIVE items. Format as a clean, high-density note with sections: '## Current Focus' (what the agent is working on), '## Active Context' (operational state, environment notes, pending items), '## Open Items' (unresolved blockers or follow-ups). The result MUST be under 2,000 characters. Use the exec tool to write the file.

STEP 10 — DEEP TRUTHS REVIEW: Review if any promoted or long-standing Core Memory facts qualify as Deep Truths. RULES: (a) Only change during this nightly consolidation, never during regular work. (b) Evidence must span 3+ separate work sessions or days. (c) The relevant fact must have been stable in Core Memory for 7+ days. (d) Must cite at least 2 Core Memory entries as evidence. (e) Must be a single concise sentence, universally applicable. (f) Use `update-deep-truths --add "<truth>"` to add, `update-deep-truths --remove "<text>"` to remove. (g) Maximum 2 changes per run, maximum 10 Deep Truths total. (h) Every addition/removal MUST include justification and cited Core Memory IDs in the report. (i) If unsure whether something qualifies, it does NOT — wait for more evidence.
context.success_criteria: MEMORY.md is rewritten to contain only active context, under 2,000 characters. Core Memory is reconciled — stale entries retired, contradicted entries superseded, and genuinely new facts promoted. Deep Truths reviewed and updated only if warranted by strong multi-session evidence. A structured report is produced covering: items triaged, retirements, promotions, Deep Truth changes, and final MEMORY.md character count.
context.prior_learnings: Be conservative with both promotions AND retirements — verify before acting. Only promote facts confirmed across multiple sessions. Only retire facts you have clear evidence are wrong or stale. Session-specific debugging notes, one-off error messages, and transient task status should be pruned from MEMORY.md, not promoted. An empty MEMORY.md (just the template header) is a valid and healthy outcome. When rewriting MEMORY.md, use the exec tool to write the file — the file_write tool may not be available in all contexts. When retiring Core Memory, always provide a specific reason — never bulk-retire without justification.

responsibilities.name: Weekly Git Artifact GC
responsibilities.instruction: Run garbage collection on git artifact repos to consolidate bundle chains. For each active project, execute: node /opt/corekit/corekit/lib/git-store.mjs gc <projectId> main. List active projects first with project-manage list. Report the number of bundles consolidated per repo.

context.purpose: Git artifact repos accumulate bundle objects in GCS as missions create, push, and merge branches. Over time, bundle chains grow long as each push adds incremental bundles. GC consolidates these chains into fewer, larger bundles to improve clone/fetch performance and reduce object count.
process: STEP 1 — LIST ACTIVE PROJECTS: Run `project-manage list` to get all active project IDs (these are the repoIds).
STEP 2 — RUN GC: For each project repo, execute `node /opt/corekit/corekit/lib/git-store.mjs gc <repoId> main`. This consolidates bundle chains by repacking incremental bundles into fewer objects.
STEP 3 — REPORT: Summarize results — repos processed, bundles consolidated per repo.
context.success_criteria: GC ran on all active project repos. Report shows repos processed and bundles consolidated per repo. No errors during consolidation.
